theme_note: Calls, layout choices, and design work build the first AMD mark and extend it with AYY, Ryzen, Radeon, and ATI; what varies is which mark and whether people are starting, enlarging, or moving it.

second_order: keeping, repairing and preserving the logos
theme_note: People reinforce borders, call backup, correct proportions, reclaim damage, and keep the artwork standing; later the same practice continues through clean copies and hand repair after shutdown.

second_order: choosing the logo's colours and trying to settle the fight
theme_note: People advocate red, green, black, or orange, poll one another, invoke votes and history, and ask for consistency; the positions vary while the shared practice is deciding what their marks should look like.

second_order: naming attackers and rallying a fight back
theme_note: Participants name Novideo supporters, Poland, r/bluecorner, r/Skyshaper, or other perceived attackers and use those claims to call defense or counterattack; the named opponent and requested response vary.

second_order: making, testing and honouring deals with neighbours
theme_note: People seek alliances, argue over whether cooperation is possible, announce truces and border bargains, repair a neighbour's flag, and thank or credit partners; relations range from threatened conflict to mutual help.

second_order: trying glitches, extra accounts, bots and scripts
theme_note: Participants test or explain ways to place more or maintain pixels, from a client-side glitch and multiple accounts to TOR accounts and automation; some are tentative proposals while others report actual use.

second_order: using petitions and heretic calls to judge people and places
theme_note: The room recruits its familiar approved, unapproved, and heretic formats to pass judgment on r/place participants and neighbours, while some replies resist turning those judgments into a witch-hunt.

second_order: pulling the subreddit's own April Fools switch
theme_note: Participants reverse ordinary loyalties, test whether others recognize the joke, and reveal the bamboozle; this is the room's own April Fools conduct and not conduct about the canvas.

second_order: celebrating and mourning what the canvas showed
theme_note: People praise a logo in good condition, celebrate what they achieved or call a sight glorious, and later register that their work is gone; the evaluations range from triumph to loss.

second_order: correcting sabotage claims and cooling fights
theme_note: Replies challenge claims of outside sabotage by pointing to infighting, voting, design reasons, or calm conditions, and redirect people away from escalation; what varies is the disputed culprit and correction.

second_order: joking that Novideo will pay for their wall
theme_note: This campaign joke answers border-building with the claim that Novideo will pay; no other code performs the same practice closely enough to group with it.
